questions.question: When driving a tractor-trailer with ABS, what should you do?

options.text: Use extra braking force to activate the ABS.
Use less braking pressure than normal.

questions.explanation: Brake the same way you would in a vehicle without ABS. The ABS system handles the rest automatically.

questions.question: When you couple glad hands, at what angle should the seals be pressed together?
questions.explanation: Press the seals together at a 90-degree angle when coupling glad hands.

questions.question: Before you back your tractor under the trailer, what should you do with the trailer brakes?
questions.explanation: Lock the trailer brakes before backing your tractor under the trailer.

questions.question: If oil and water build up in your air tanks, what happens to the brakes?
questions.explanation: Drain air tanks daily to remove water and oil. Too much buildup can stop the brakes from working properly.

questions.question: Trailers with low clearance underneath are hard to drive:
questions.explanation: Raised railroad crossings are hard to cross with low-slung trailers. Single-axle tractors pulling long trailers have extra difficulty.

questions.question: After coupling, how much space should there be between the upper and lower fifth wheel?
questions.explanation: There should be no space between the upper and lower fifth wheel after coupling.

questions.question: If you cannot back your trailer straight, which direction should you back?
questions.explanation: Back on a curved path toward the driver's side. This gives you the best view while backing.

questions.question: After you finish a pre-trip inspection, what should you do?

options.text: Leave the emergency line valve open
Leave the rear shut-off valves open

questions.explanation: Close both shut-off valves before you drive. Open them first to check that air reaches all brakes, then close them.

questions.question: While inspecting a coupling, you should go under the trailer and:

options.text: Detach the jaws from the kingpin
Put the locking lever in the "emergency" position
Look into the back of the fifth wheel

questions.correctAnswerText: Look into the back of the fifth wheel
questions.explanation: Look into the back of the fifth wheel and make sure the jaws are locked around the kingpin.

questions.question: What is a tractor protection valve?

options.text: A device that keeps air in the tractor brakes if the trailer breaks away or leaks badly
A device that controls fuel levels
A device that helps the battery recharge

questions.correctAnswerText: A device that keeps air in the tractor brakes if the trailer breaks away or leaks badly
questions.explanation: The tractor protection valve keeps air in the tractor brakes. It works if the trailer breaks away or develops a bad leak.

questions.question: If a trailer begins to skid, what should the driver do?
questions.explanation: When a trailer skids while braking, release the brakes to let the wheels grip the road again. Once traction returns, the trailer will straighten out and follow the tractor.

questions.question: Changing lanes quickly can cause:

options.text: A "crack-the-whip" effect that can cause a rollover.
Confusion about which lane the driver wants.

questions.correctAnswerText: A "crack-the-whip" effect that can cause a rollover.
questions.explanation: The "crack-the-whip" effect happens when you change lanes too quickly with a trailer. This can cause the trailer to roll over.

questions.question: What happens when a trailer's wheels lock up?

options.text: The trailer continues in a straight line.

questions.explanation: When a trailer's wheels lock up, the trailer tends to swing around. This can cause a jackknife.

questions.question: What is a tractor protection valve?

options.text: A valve that keeps air in the brake system if there is a leak.
A valve that prevents the truck from being stolen.
A valve that prevents the driver from speeding.
A valve that prevents the trailer from disconnecting.

questions.correctAnswerText: A valve that keeps air in the brake system if there is a leak.
questions.explanation: The tractor protection valve keeps air in the tractor's brake system if the trailer breaks away or develops a leak.

questions.question: A shut-off valve:

options.text: Is located on the front of a trailer.
Stops air from leaving the brake system.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stops air from leaving the brake system.
questions.explanation: Shut-off valves control air flow between trailers. The rear shut-off valve should stay closed to prevent air from leaving the braking system.

questions.question: Air pressure in the ____ air line is controlled by the foot brake or trailer hand brake.
questions.explanation: The service air line (also called the control line or signal line) is controlled by the foot brake or trailer hand brake. It connects to relay valves, which apply the trailer brakes quickly.

questions.question: Compared to empty rigs, fully-loaded rigs:

options.text: Are less likely to roll over.
Are more likely to roll over.
Are just as likely to roll over.

questions.correctAnswerText: Are more likely to roll over.
questions.explanation: Fully-loaded rigs have a higher center of gravity because of the cargo weight. They are 10 times more likely to roll over in a crash than empty rigs.

questions.question: Pull out the trailer air supply control to test:
questions.explanation: Test the trailer emergency brakes before starting a trip. Pull out the trailer air supply control or set it to "emergency." Pull forward slightly with the tractor. The trailer should not move.

questions.question: To prevent a rollover, a driver should:
questions.explanation: Rollovers happen when you turn too quickly. Keep the center of gravity low by loading cargo as close to the ground as possible to reduce rollover risk.

questions.question: The service air line connects to the:
questions.explanation: The service air line carries air controlled by the foot brake or trailer hand brake. It connects to relay valves, which apply the trailer brakes quickly.
